# Awesome NVIDIA Physical-Simulation Infrastructure [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re) > A curated list of resources for NVIDIA's modular physical-simulation stack — spanning OpenUSD, Omniverse, DSX, robotics, and CAE/CFD workflows. This list is organized around a **layered infrastructure** view of the stack, not as a single monolithic platform. The insight: NVIDIA's industrial significance lies in connecting **interoperable scene data**, **GPU-native simulation**, and **blueprint-packaged deployment** — not in any single simulator alone.

--- ## Open Research Paper — Call for Co-Authors This repository is accompanied by a **working paper** currently in draft: > **[From OpenUSD to DSX: NVIDIA's Modular Physical-Simulation Infrastructure for Digital Twins, Robotics, and AI Factories](paper/draft.md)** **We're actively seeking co-authors and contributors.** If you work on any part of this stack — at NVIDIA, at a partner company, in research, or in open-source — your perspective would strengthen the analysis. See [`paper/CALL_FOR_AUTHORS.md`](paper/CALL_FOR_AUTHORS.md) for details. | Area | What's Needed | |------|---------------| | OpenUSD standards & AOUSD | Governance process, spec evolution, cross-vendor adoption data | | DSX deployment | Production experiences, scaling observations, integration patterns | | Robotics (Isaac Sim / Lab / OSMO) | Sim-to-real transfer results, benchmark comparisons, workflow reviews | | CAE / CFD digital twins | PhysicsNeMo surrogate model accuracy, Kit-CAE production readiness | | Newton & Warp | Differentiable simulation use cases, performance benchmarking | | Competitor/alternative analysis | Comparison with Unity, MuJoCo, Gazebo, AWS IoT TwinMaker, Azure Digital Twins | --- ## Why This List Exists Physical AI, industrial digital twins, and AI-factory operations all place new pressure on simulation systems. The challenge is no longer just running a physics kernel quickly — it's organizing data exchange, scene composition, simulation services, delivery, and vertical deployment so multiple teams can work on a shared operational model. ``` +-----------------------------------------------------+ | Vertical Workflows DSX . Robotics . CAE/CFD | +-----------------------------------------------------+ | Delivery & Orchestration App Streaming . Helm | +-----------------------------------------------------+ | Runtime & App Construction Kit SDK . Libraries | +-----------------------------------------------------+ | Acceleration & Simulation Warp.PhysX.RTX.Newton | +-----------------------------------------------------+ | Interoperability & Semantics OpenUSD . SimReady | +-----------------------------------------------------+ ``` --- ## Contents - [Layer 1: Interoperability & Semantics](#layer-1-interoperability--semantics) - [Layer 2: Acceleration & Simulation](#layer-2-acceleration--simulation) - [Layer 3: Runtime & Application Construction](#layer-3-runtime--application-construction) - [Layer 4: Delivery & Orchestration](#layer-4-delivery--orchestration) - [Layer 5: Vertical Workflows & Blueprints](#layer-5-vertical-workflows--blueprints) - [Cross-Cutting Topics](#cross-cutting-topics) - [Timeline & Ecosystem Evolution](#timeline--ecosystem-evolution) - [Community Projects & Integrations](#community-projects--integrations) - [Ecosystem Landscape](#ecosystem-landscape) - [Learning Paths](#learning-paths) - [Contributing](#contributing) --- ## Layer 1: Interoperability & Semantics OpenUSD is not a file format — it's the shared scene and composition substrate that lets data and semantics move through the entire stack. ### OpenUSD Core - [OpenUSD Official Site](https://openusd.org/) — Specification, API reference, and community resources - [OpenUSD GitHub](https://github.com/PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD) — Pixar's reference implementation - [OpenUSD Core Specification 1.0](https://aousd.org/news/core-spec-announcement/) — Ratified December 2025 by AOUSD, the formal standards base for scene composition - [USD FAQ](https://openusd.org/22.08/usdfaq.html) — Covers stages, layers, and composition arcs - [How to Use OpenUSD](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/how-to-use-openusd/) — NVIDIA's developer-oriented guide to authoring and composition workflows ### OpenUSD Exchange SDK - [Exchange SDK Documentation](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/usd/code-docs/usd-exchange-sdk/latest/index.html) — Tools for ingest and interchange across upstream design tools (CAD, DCC, etc.) - [Connect Samples](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/connect-samples) — Reference code for building OpenUSD connectors ### SimReady Assets & Schemas - [SimReady Overview](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/simready/latest/index.html) — OpenUSD-based building blocks with metadata, semantics, sensor attributes, and physical properties - [SimReady Asset Specification](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/simready/latest/overview/simready-spec.html) — Technical specification for simulation-ready assets - [SimReady Explorer](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/extensions/latest/ext_core/ext_browser-extensions/simready-explorer.html) — Browse and discover SimReady assets ### Alliance for OpenUSD (AOUSD) - [AOUSD Official Site](https://aousd.org/) — The industry alliance driving OpenUSD standardization - [Core Spec 1.0 Blog](https://aousd.org/blog/foundations-of-open-3d-development-introducing-aousd-core-specification-1-0/) — Context on the ratification and what it means for the ecosystem --- ## Layer 2: Acceleration & Simulation GPU-native simulation substrate: engines that compute physics, rendering, and domain-specific solvers. ### Warp - [NVIDIA Warp](https://developer.nvidia.com/warp-python) — Python framework for GPU simulation and spatial computing - [Warp GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/warp) — Source code, examples, and documentation. Differentiable kernels work with PyTorch, JAX, and Paddle - [Warp Documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/warp/) — API reference, tutorials, and differentiable simulation examples - [Warp Publications](https://github.com/NVIDIA/warp/blob/main/PUBLICATIONS.md) — Academic and research papers leveraging Warp ### PhysX - [PhysX 5 SDK](https://developer.nvidia.com/physx-sdk) — GPU-accelerated rigid body, soft body, fluid, and cloth simulation - [PhysX GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/PhysX) — Open-source SDK ### RTX & Rendering - [RTX Renderer Documentation](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/materials-and-rendering/latest/rtx-renderer.html) — Real-time and path-traced rendering in the Omniverse stack ### Newton - [Newton GitHub](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton) — GPU-accelerated physics engine built on Warp, targeting roboticists and simulation researchers. Extends Warp's warp.sim module and integrates MuJoCo Warp - [Newton Developer Page](https://developer.nvidia.com/newton-physics) — Official NVIDIA page ### PhysicsNeMo - [PhysicsNeMo GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/physicsnemo) — Open-source framework for building, training, and fine-tuning physics-ML models (CFD, structural mechanics, electromagnetics) - [Earth-2 Studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio) — Inference sub-module for climate and weather AI models ### CUDA-X & Domain Solvers - [CUDA-X Libraries](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpu-accelerated-libraries) — GPU-accelerated libraries for linear algebra, FFT, signal processing, and more --- ## Layer 3: Runtime & Application Construction The developer-facing layer for building applications and headless services. ### Kit SDK - [Kit SDK Overview](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/dev-guide/latest/overview.html) — Developer guide for building Omniverse applications - [Kit 106.0 Release Highlights](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/dev-guide/latest/release-notes/106_0_highlights.html) — The May 2024 pivot toward developer-facing infrastructure - [Kit App Template GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/kit-app-template) — Official starter for custom Kit applications ### Omniverse Libraries - [Omniverse Libraries Overview](https://developer.nvidia.com/omniverse) — Modular libraries including ovrtx, ovphysx, and more - [Platform Overview](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/dev-overview/latest/platform-overview.html) — How libraries, SDKs, services, and blueprints compose into the platform - [Introduction — Developer Overview](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/dev-overview/latest/introduction.html) — Omniverse as a development stack for 3D applications at scale ### Extensions - [Extensions Documentation](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/extensions/latest/index.html) — Discover and build Kit extensions --- ## Layer 4: Delivery & Orchestration How simulation applications reach users — from GPU servers to browsers. ### App Streaming - [App Streaming Documentation](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/kit-app-template/108.0/docs/streaming.html) — Stream Kit applications via WebRTC to browsers and thin clients ### Containerization & Helm - [Omniverse Container Deployment](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/ovas/latest/deployments/index.html) — Container and Helm-based deployment for production workloads ### Orchestration - [NVIDIA OSMO GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OSMO) — Developer-first platform for scaling Physical AI workloads across heterogeneous compute (training GPUs, simulation clusters, edge devices) in YAML. Powers Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim, and Project GR00T at scale --- ## Layer 5: Vertical Workflows & Blueprints NVIDIA Blueprints package the stack into reusable, domain-oriented workflows. ### DSX — AI Factories & Data Centers > DSX is the strongest full-stack case: shared OpenUSD scene data, domain simulations, App Streaming, multi-role review, and blueprint packaging in one reference workflow. - [DSX Blueprint Overview](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/dsx/latest/overview.html) — 50-acre AI-factory geometry set, thermal/electrical simulations, multi-role workflow - [DSX Blueprint GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse-blueprints/omniverse-dsx-blueprint-for-ai-factories) — Source code, web stack, and deployment documentation - [DSX Launch Blog](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/omniverse-dsx-blueprint/) — Gigawatt-scale AI factory digital twins - [Vera Rubin DSX Announcement](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-releases-vera-rubin-dsx-ai-factory-reference-design-and-omniverse-dsx-digital-twin-blueprint-with-broad-industry-support) — GA release with broad industry support (March 2026) ### Robotics — Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab & OSMO - [Isaac Sim](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/sim) — Open-source reference framework for robotics simulation, testing, and synthetic data generation - [Isaac Sim GitHub](https://github.com/isaac-sim) — Source repositories - [Isaac Lab GitHub](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab) — GPU-accelerated unified framework for robot learning (RL, imitation learning, motion planning). 6.8k+ stars - [Isaac Lab Arena](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena) — Composable, scalable system for diverse simulation environments - [OSMO](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OSMO) — Orchestration for the full Physical AI pipeline: training, simulation, hardware testing ### CAE / CFD — Kit-CAE & Physics Digital Twins - [Kit-CAE Guide](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/guide-kit-cae/latest/index.html) — Combining NVIDIA technologies for CAE data (CGNS, NPZ schemas) - [Physics Digital Twin Blueprint Blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/rapidly-create-real-time-physics-digital-twins-with-nvidia-omniverse-blueprints/) — Omniverse APIs + PhysicsNeMo + App Streaming + reference deployment ### Other NVIDIA Blueprints - [NVIDIA Omniverse Blueprints GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse-blueprints) — Open-source physical-simulation blueprints (DSX and more) - [NVIDIA AI Blueprints GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA-AI-Blueprints) — Open-source AI/agentic blueprints (RAG, digital human, drug discovery, retail, and more) - *Contributions welcome — see [Contributing](#contributing)* --- ## Cross-Cutting Topics ### Differentiable Simulation - [Warp Differentiable Simulation](https://nvidia.github.io/warp/) — Differentiable physics for optimization and learning - [Newton](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton) — Integrates MuJoCo Warp for differentiable rigid body simulation - *Contributions welcome for research papers and benchmarks* ### Capture-to-Simulation Pipelines - [Neural Reconstruction in Isaac Sim](https://developer.nvidia.com/isaac/sim) — Capture-to-USD pipelines for robotics - *Contributions welcome for NeRF/3DGS to OpenUSD tools* ### Agentic Operations & NIM - [NVIDIA NIM](https://developer.nvidia.com/nim) — Inference microservices composable with simulation workflows - *Contributions welcome* --- ## Timeline & Ecosystem Evolution | Date | Milestone | |------|-----------| | May 2024 | Kit 106 pivots toward developer-facing infrastructure | | Aug 2024 | NIM Agent Blueprints launch as customizable workflows | | Oct 2024 | "NVIDIA Blueprints" becomes the lasting umbrella term | | Nov 2024 | CAE digital twin blueprint makes vertical packaging explicit | | Oct 2025 | DSX blueprint introduced for gigawatt-scale AI factories | | Dec 2025 | OpenUSD Core Specification 1.0 ratified by AOUSD | | Mar 2026 | DSX blueprint reaches general availability | | Mar 2026 | NVIDIA OSMO open-sourced for Physical AI orchestration | --- ## Community Projects & Integrations > **This is where your project goes.** If you're building on any layer of this stack, submit a PR! ### Related Awesome Lists - [awesome-isaac-gym](https://github.com/robotlearning123/awesome-isaac-gym) — Curated list of Isaac Gym frameworks, papers, and resources - [Awesome-Physical-Engineering-AI](https://github.com/010zx00x1/Awesome-Physical-Engineering-AI) — AI tools for hardware engineering, CAD, simulation, and manufacturing - [awesome-robotics-libraries](https://github.com/jslee02/awesome-robotics-libraries) — Comprehensive list of robotics simulators and libraries - [Awesome-Physics-aware-Generation](https://github.com/BestJunYu/Awesome-Physics-aware-Generation) — Physics-aware generative modeling papers ### OpenUSD Tools & Converters - *Your project here* ### Digital Twin Implementations - *Your project here* ### Simulation Workflows & Extensions - *Your project here* ### Deployment & Infrastructure - *Your project here* --- ## Ecosystem Landscape How NVIDIA's stack relates to adjacent platforms and alternatives. | Layer | NVIDIA Stack | Alternatives / Complements | |-------|-------------|---------------------------| | Scene standard | OpenUSD | glTF, FBX, STEP | | Physics engine | PhysX, Newton, Warp | MuJoCo, Bullet, DART, Chrono | | Robot sim | Isaac Sim / Lab | Gazebo, MuJoCo MPC, PyBullet, SAPIEN | | Digital twins | DSX, Kit-CAE | Azure Digital Twins, AWS IoT TwinMaker, Eclipse Ditto | | Orchestration | OSMO | Kubernetes + custom, Airflow | | AI surrogates | PhysicsNeMo | DeepXDE, custom PINN frameworks | | Rendering | RTX | Vulkan, OptiX, Embree | --- ## Learning Paths ### Getting Started - [ ] Understand [OpenUSD composition arcs](https://openusd.org/22.08/usdfaq.html) — stages, layers, sublayers, references, payloads, variants - [ ] Set up [Kit SDK](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/dev-guide/latest/overview.html) and build a first extension - [ ] Explore [SimReady assets](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/simready/latest/index.html) and understand simulation-ready metadata - [ ] Try [Warp](https://github.com/NVIDIA/warp) for GPU-accelerated Python simulation ### Intermediate - [ ] Build a custom Kit application using the [App Template](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse/kit-app-template) - [ ] Deploy a streamed application using [App Streaming](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/kit-app-template/108.0/docs/streaming.html) - [ ] Run the [DSX Blueprint](https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse-blueprints/omniverse-dsx-blueprint-for-ai-factories) locally - [ ] Orchestrate a multi-step Physical AI pipeline with [OSMO](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OSMO) ### Advanced - [ ] Compose multi-domain simulations using OpenUSD composition arcs - [ ] Integrate [PhysicsNeMo](https://github.com/NVIDIA/physicsnemo) surrogate models into a digital twin workflow - [ ] Build and deploy a custom NVIDIA Blueprint for your vertical - [ ] Contribute to the [working paper](paper/CALL_FOR_AUTHORS.md) --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome and encouraged! See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed guidelines. **What we're looking for:** - Official documentation, blog posts, and tutorials - Open-source projects building on any layer of the stack - Real-world case studies and deployment experiences - Learning resources — tutorials, courses, videos - Research papers on differentiable simulation, capture-to-sim, agentic operations, or OpenUSD - Industry integrations and connectors - **[Paper co-authorship](paper/CALL_FOR_AUTHORS.md)** — help refine the architecture analysis --- ## License [![CC0](https://licensebuttons.net/p/zero/1.0/88x31.png)](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) This list is released under [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).
